raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #1736.

**1. Gate `short_tile_opt` on the persistent scheduler.** `short_tile_opt` (shared first softmax step + single-stage epilogue) was gated only on the sparse-index capacity. With a **fixed top-k** (no `q2k_block_nums`) the wrapper uses the static one-tile-per-CTA scheduler unless `tiles >= 8192 and top-k >= 256` or `top-k <= 128` with enough tiles (`choose_blk64_use_clc`). On that scheduler the single-stage epilogue is already off (it needs the persistent path) and the only thing left, the shared first softmax step, has no per-tile ramp to overlap and is a net loss: **5-12% slower** on several MiniMax-H3 shapes. My #1736 measurements always passed per-row counts, i.e. always ran on CLC, so this path was not covered. `short_tile_opt` is now additionally gated on `is_persistent` (host-side, no sync); with the flag off the kernel is code-identical to before #1736.

**2. Drop the redundant `not self.is_split_kv` from `epi_single_stage`.** Split-KV always writes FP32 O partials, so `o_dtype == BFloat16` already excludes it; the term never changed the generated kernel.

## Measurement (B300, `benchmark_bsa_minimax_h3.py` h3 suite, B=1, H=7, D=128, BF16, blk64)

API-level timing as in that script (CUDA events around the public call, L2 flushed per sample, 5 warmup + 20 runs per round), 3 interleaved rounds per case (before/after order alternates), median of the three round medians. Top-k routing of mean-pooled Q.K, per-row counts = the table's average KV tiles. "before" = kernel of 2f5e93c00~1, "after" = kernel of #1736 (left) and with change 1 (right). Scheduler = what `choose_blk64_use_clc` picks.

| case (Sq, density) | scheduler | #1736 vs before | this PR vs before |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5s (38,247) 15% | CLC | 0.831 -> 0.802 ms (-3.5%) | 0.836 -> 0.789 ms (-5.6%) |
| 5s 30% | static | 1.521 -> 1.705 (**+12.1%**) | 1.620 -> 1.622 (+0.1%) |
| 5s 50% | static | 2.673 -> 2.987 (**+11.8%**) | 2.713 -> 2.698 (-0.6%) |
| 5s 100% | static (flag off) | 4.809 -> 4.831 (+0.5%) | 4.947 -> 4.812 (-2.7%) |
| 10s (68,487) 15% | static | 2.676 -> 2.887 (**+7.9%**) | 2.741 -> 2.763 (+0.8%) |
| 10s 30% | static | 5.197 -> 5.521 (**+6.2%**) | 5.278 -> 5.137 (-2.7%) |
| 10s 50% | static | 8.583 -> 9.043 (**+5.4%**) | 8.523 -> 8.379 (-1.7%) |
| 10s 100% | static | 15.590 -> 15.589 (0.0%) | 15.598 -> 15.583 (-0.1%) |
| 15s (98,727) 15% | static | 5.736 -> 6.058 (**+5.6%**) | 5.718 -> 5.631 (-1.5%) |
| 15s 30% | CLC | 10.414 -> 10.360 (-0.5%) | 10.444 -> 10.361 (-0.8%) |
| 15s 50% | CLC | 16.883 -> 16.796 (-0.5%) | 16.889 -> 16.809 (-0.5%) |
| 15s 100% | static | 30.448 -> 30.445 (0.0%) | 30.451 -> 30.437 (0.0%) |

Round-to-round spread on this machine (clocks not locked) is a few percent, up to ~10% in the worst rounds, so differences within about +/-3% are noise; the static cases with this change run the same compiled kernel as "before". Sampled fp32 reference check of O and LSE on every case: max |err| <= 1.8e-4. The CLC cases (5s/15%, 15s/30-50%) keep the #1736 behaviour.

Why the gate needs `is_persistent` and not just a different capacity threshold: on the static scheduler with the h3 shapes, each optimization on its own (7 interleaved rounds per case, B300) gives single-stage epilogue alone -2.3..+0.6%, shared first softmax step alone **+6.5..+15.9%**, both together +0.6..+3.2%, all with O and LSE bit-identical to the baseline.

## Testing

`test_BSA_attention_forward.py -k sm100` + `test_BSA_attention_fp8.py`: 64 passed (against the package change 1 was measured with; the `develop` test files could not be run on the machine because its compiled extension predates `cudnn.ops`). Change 2 only drops a compile-time constant that is already false whenever it would have mattered, so it was not separately re-run.

@@ -1991,9 +1991,11 @@ def bsa_attn_fwd_blk64_cutedsl(
     is_persistent = use_clc_scheduler
     pack_gqa = False
     input_layout = "bhsd_native"
-    # Short/medium KV lists are dominated by the per-tile ramp, which short_tile_opt shortens; near-dense lists (capacity of the
-    # sparse index >= 90% of the KV blocks, known on the host without a sync) hide the ramp and keep the original schedule.
-    short_tile_opt = int(q2k_block_index.shape[-1]) * 10 < ((seqlen_k + sparse_block_size - 1) // sparse_block_size) * 9
+    # Short/medium KV lists on the persistent (CLC) scheduler are dominated by the per-tile ramp, which short_tile_opt shortens.
+    # Near-dense lists (capacity of the sparse index >= 90% of the KV blocks, known on the host without a sync) hide the ramp, and
+    # the static one-tile-per-CTA scheduler has no ramp to overlap (the shared first softmax step is a net loss there): both keep
+    # the original schedule.
+    short_tile_opt = is_persistent and int(q2k_block_index.shape[-1]) * 10 < ((seqlen_k + sparse_block_size - 1) // sparse_block_size) * 9
 
     split_offsets = None
     if kv_splits_i > 1:

@@ -305,9 +305,7 @@ def __call__(
         self.is_sage_fp8 = mQScale is not None
         # The persistent BF16 path keeps the epilogue exchange buffer + sO inside ONE KV smem stage (two column
         # passes of 32 KB), so the next tile's K0/K1 can be prefetched into the other two stages.
-        self.epi_single_stage = (
-            self.short_tile_opt and self.is_persistent and not self.is_sage_fp8 and not self.is_split_kv and self.o_dtype == cutlass.BFloat16
-        )
+        self.epi_single_stage = self.short_tile_opt and self.is_persistent and not self.is_sage_fp8 and self.o_dtype == cutlass.BFloat16

             self.epi_exchange_f32_count = 2 * 4 * 32 * 32
         self.epi_sO_input_offset = self.epi_exchange_f32_count * (Float32.width // self.k_dtype.width)

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `e988a309ba90` against base `dfd53ef14eb7`.

No blocking findings. Restricting the short-tile specialization to the persistent scheduler is consistent with the intended optimization, and the compile key already distinguishes that flag. The split-KV wrapper always allocates FP32 partial outputs, so removing its redundant BF16-epilogue exclusion does not enable that epilogue for supported split calls.

Validation: Exact-head local SM100 run with Torch 2.14.1 and CuTe DSL 4.8.0: 38 forward tests passed, explicitly including L1 static/persistent changed-input replay, partial blocks, empty variable-count queries, split-KV and numerical-extreme controls; the FP8 suite added 28 passes. Baseline/head comparison used the actual two changed files from 7089f1182761 and e988a309ba90, with identical inputs and unchanged supporting code. Four native cases covered static fixed-count, CLC fixed-count, CLC variable-count and CLC split-KV. Output/LSE comparisons and independent sampled FP32 references passed; maximum sampled output error was 4.25e-4. Repeated graph replay was bitwise stable in these cases. Five interleaved warm CUDA Graph replay rounds on an SM100 engineering GPU: median baseline/head times were 3360.9/3399.1 us (static), 265.9/266.7 us (CLC fixed), 71.53/71.13 us (CLC variable), and 172.46/172.51 us (CLC split). No material regression was established. A follow-up with alternating, individually drained warm CLC calls measured host enqueue medians of 54.06/53.56 us; the initial batched host measurements were noisy. Existing current-head pipeline 76914007 already has successful SM100, SM90 and SM107 CuTeDSL lanes; SM80 is still pending. Reused the author's run without triggering a duplicate.

Limitations: The local GPU is an SM100 engineering device, not B300. These warm replay spot checks do not reproduce the author's flushed-cache API benchmark or establish its B300 speedup. No new sanitizer run or end-to-end model benchmark for this small scheduling gate; repeatability evidence is limited to the four fixed configurations above.
